But this is a plain util function, not a component, so it cannot call the hook directly — the caller would need to pass isMobile in, or the function should read it from a shared snapshot. The touch part is already covered by useBreakpoint().isTouch; only the UA-keyword part is extra.

detections.detects: Phone-sized viewport inside checkIsMobile(), which feeds the AI device-capability tier (HIGH/MID/LEGACY/UNSUPPORTED) alongside WebGPU, deviceMemory, UA version parsing.
detections.migration: The bare width<768 check equals useBreakpoint().isMobile and isTouch equals useBreakpoint().isTouch. However this lives in the device-capability / AI-tier path, which also models GPU/WebGPU, deviceMemory, data-saver, and Android/iOS version parsing — none of which useBreakpoint covers. Do not fold the whole function into the hook; at most swap the width literal for the shared breakpoint when a component owns the call.

detections.detects: Viewport narrower than sm/640px to gate a 'screen too small' warning modal.
detections.migration: This is a React component, so it is a clean swap: const { width } = useBreakpoint(); then `if (dismissed || width >= 640) return null;` (or `bp !== 'base'` to mean >= xs... but 640 is sm, so compare width >= 640 / BREAKPOINTS.sm). Bonus: the hook re-renders on resize, so the warning would now react live to rotation/resize instead of only the first render.

detections.code:
const screenWidth = Math.max(window.screen.width, window.screen.height);
  const isTabletScreenSize = screenWidth >= 768 && screenWidth <= 1366;
detections.detects: Tablet-class physical SCREEN size (largest dimension 768-1366) combined with UA/platform sniffing (iPad, Android tablet, Surface, maxTouchPoints>2) to label the device a tablet.
detections.migration: useBreakpoint models the VIEWPORT (window.innerWidth/Height), not the physical screen (window.screen.width/height). It exposes isTablet = width in [768,1024), which is a different and narrower band than this 768-1366 screen-size heuristic, and it has no UA/platform tablet sniffing (iPad-as-Mac, Surface). Cannot reproduce this classification from useBreakpoint.

detections.detects: User-agent / platform mobile+tablet sniffing (iPad, Android tablet, Surface) to choose the notice text.
detections.migration: useBreakpoint has no userAgent sniffing — only isTouch (ontouchstart / maxTouchPoints>0) and viewport width buckets. It cannot tell an iPad from an Android tablet or a Surface. Not migratable.

detections.detects: Re-runs the tablet check on viewport resize so the notice updates on rotation/resize — a hand-rolled resize listener for layout.
detections.migration: useBreakpoint already owns one shared resize + orientationchange listener and re-renders consumers. If the tablet decision were viewport-based you would drop this listener entirely and read the hook. Here the decision is screen-size + UA based (see lines 13/27), so the listener is only re-triggering UA/screen logic the hook does not model — the listener itself is redundant with the hook's, but the work it does is not.

detections.code:

  const isTabletScreenSize = screenWidth >= 768 && screenWidth <= 1366;
detections.detects: Identical tablet physical-SCREEN-size heuristic (768-1366) inside isTabletDevice(), combined with UA/platform sniffing, used to pick the storage strategy (File System API vs IndexedDB+download).
detections.migration: Same as MobileNotice: this is window.screen (physical screen), not the viewport useBreakpoint reads, plus UA/platform sniffing the hook has none of. useBreakpoint().isTablet is a 768-1024 viewport band, not equivalent. Also this is a non-component util that cannot call the hook. Not migratable.

detections.detects: Landscape orientation of the viewport inside getOrientationInfo().
detections.migration: Equivalent to useBreakpoint().isLandscape (width >= height). Caveat: the hook uses >= (square counts as landscape) while this uses strict > (square counts as portrait) — a 1px edge-case difference. Still a non-component util, so it cannot call the hook directly; a component caller would pass isLandscape in.

detections.detects: Raw viewport width/height returned in the getOrientationInfo() payload (consumed by PacketPersistence for an orientation badge).
detections.migration: Equivalent to useBreakpoint().width and .height. Same constraint: util function, not a hook context; a component would read width/height from the hook and pass them down.

detections.detects: Hand-rolled resize + orientationchange listener that refreshes storageInfo.orientation (via getOrientationInfo) so the UI reflects rotation.
detections.migration: This duplicates exactly the listener pair inside useBreakpoint (resize + orientationchange). The component could consume useBreakpoint() for {width,height,isLandscape} and drop both addEventListener calls and the manual cleanup. Blocked only because the orientation data also flows through getOrientationInfo()'s UA-based screenType ('tablet'/'phone'/'desktop'), which the hook does not model; the width/height/landscape half is a clean swap.

detections.detects: Resize listener that re-measures the SVG container via containerRef.getBoundingClientRect() to size the D3 graph. Tracks element box, not the window viewport.
detections.migration: Not a viewport-breakpoint listener — it measures a specific DOM element's box (getBoundingClientRect), which useBreakpoint does not provide (the hook only knows window.innerWidth/Height). The correct consolidation target is a ResizeObserver on the element, not useBreakpoint. Leave as-is for this task.

detections.detects: Reads viewport width/height to center the draggable assistant panel on first open (no saved position).
detections.migration: width/height are available as useBreakpoint().width/.height. But this is a one-shot computation inside a useState initializer for absolute pixel math (centering), not a breakpoint decision; calling the hook here adds a re-rendering subscription for a value only needed once. Low value, and it is arithmetic the hook does not simplify.

detections.code:
const maxX = window.innerWidth - width;
      const maxY = window.innerHeight - height;
detections.detects: Reads live viewport size during a drag to clamp the panel inside the visible area.
detections.migration: Could read useBreakpoint().width/.height, but this runs inside a synchronous mousemove handler that needs the instantaneous value; the hook's state can lag a frame behind during fast drags and it would also force re-renders. Viewport-clamp math, not a breakpoint — keep window.innerWidth/Height here.

detections.detects: Reads viewport height to anchor the minimized/expanded launcher near the bottom of the screen.
detections.migration: useBreakpoint().height holds the same value, but this is absolute positioning arithmetic, not a breakpoint check. Substituting the hook adds a subscription without removing the need for the literal pixel math. Not a meaningful consolidation.

detections.detects: Computes the OS scrollbar gutter width (layout-viewport vs document client width) to pad the body and avoid layout shift when locking scroll.
detections.migration: useBreakpoint exposes window.innerWidth but NOT document.documentElement.clientWidth, so it cannot compute scrollbar width. This is a scrollbar-gutter measurement, unrelated to breakpoints. Not migratable.

detections.detects: User's OS reduced-motion accessibility preference (initial value).
detections.migration: Not a viewport query — it is a prefers-reduced-motion media feature. useBreakpoint models only viewport size/orientation/touch and exposes no media-preference state. Not migratable.

Guard at SmallScreenWarning.jsx:15: `if (dismissed || window.innerWidth >= 640) return null;`. smallScreenWarning.copy: Heading: "Screen Size Warning". Body paragraph 1: "VetRate is optimized for tablet and desktop screens. Some features may not work properly on smaller devices." Body paragraph 2: "For the best experience, please use a device with a screen width of at least 640px, or switch to landscape mode." Primary button: "I Understand, Continue Anyway". Secondary link: "Email Us About Mobile Support" (mailto:support@vetrate.org?subject=Mobile%20Support%20Request).
smallScreenWarning.removalGate: Deletion is GATED on the mobile e2e suite being green across the top-20 surfaces at the S10 exit (docs/SPRINT_PLAN_S9-S17.md lines 53, 67, 100). 'Green' here means tests/e2e/mobile.spec.ts passes under the mobile-chrome project (Pixel 5, 393px) plus the pinned 360px and 768px viewports, where per surface: root scrollWidth <= clientWidth+1 (no horizontal overflow); every primary CTA's getBoundingClientRect().bottom <= innerHeight (visible, not clipped by the 70px MobileBottomNav); all tap targets >= 44x44px; and the same assertions re-run inside each top-20 modal after dispatching its open* event. The mobile-chrome CI job must also be promoted to blocking. The gate exists explicitly because removing the warning early would re-expose still-broken mobile UI as 'supported' (line 100). Honest limit per the plan: real iOS Safari URL-bar/notch and screen-reader gesture checks stay owner-run manual items, not part of the automated 'green'.

mobileNotice.currentBehavior: A dismissible top banner (gradient bar) rendered by AppShellTop (e:\VS_Studio\vet-rate-org-official\src\features\app-shell\AppShellTop.jsx:39), which App.jsx renders above the header. It computes a deviceType via the isTablet() UA/screen heuristic (iPad incl. iPadOS-as-Mac, Android non-Mobile, Surface/Windows touch, or maxTouchPoints>2 within 768-1366px). After S9, the phone path is intentionally silenced: checkDevice sets deviceType to 'tablet' or null only (MobileNotice.jsx:65, with the explanatory comment at lines 59-63). So in practice only the blue tablet banner can appear; it shows once per session (dismissal persisted in sessionStorage key 'vetrate-mobile-notice-dismissed') and re-evaluates on window resize. Consequence: the entire isPhone branch (the emerald banner and the '90% of veterans' copy at lines 100-105) is now dead/unreachable code, since deviceType is never 'phone'.
mobileNotice.copyIssues: The dead phone branch still contains the contradiction the plan calls out (docs/SPRINT_PLAN_S9-S17.md line 19 'two contradictory banners'): phone copy reads "Mobile-Optimized Experience!" / "90% of veterans use mobile - this app is built for you" (lines 102-104), which directly contradicts SmallScreenWarning's standing message that screens below 640px are NOT properly supported. Both could otherwise fire on the same small device, telling the veteran simultaneously that the app is built for their phone and that their phone may break. Secondary issue: the aria-label at line 95 still maps isPhone to 'Mobile optimized', and the surviving tablet copy ("Tablet Mode - Perfect for Detailed Work!" / "Tablet screens are ideal for reviewing claims & building your packet") remains positive marketing, which is fine for tablets (>=768px, not warned) but the now-unreachable phone strings remain a latent re-introduction risk if anyone flips deviceType back on without reconciling copy.
mobileNotice.reconciliation: Reconcile copy as scheduled in S10 (lines 53, 67), tied to the same green-suite gate that removes SmallScreenWarning. Concretely: (1) delete the dead isPhone branch entirely (the emerald banner, the '90% of veterans... built for you' lines, and the isPhone-conditional aria-label/emoji), collapsing MobileNotice to the tablet-only notice it now is, so the false 'built for you' claim cannot be re-exposed; or (2) keep a phone branch only after the mobile suite is green, and at that point replace the contradictory '90% / built for you' copy with honest, non-conflicting wording and remove SmallScreenWarning in the same change so the two banners can never co-assert opposite messages. Until the gate is met, the correct state is exactly today's: phone banner silent, tablet notice kept, SmallScreenWarning retained. The minimal immediate cleanup is option (1) - prune the unreachable phone code so the contradictory copy no longer ships in the bundle, leaving SmallScreenWarning as the single source of truth for small-screen messaging until S10 removes it.

ci.mobileProjectNow: The `mobile-chrome` project (playwright.config.ts:27-30) is defined as `use: { ...devices["Pixel 5"] }` — Pixel 5 emulation (~393x851, mobile UA, touch). It is one of three projects (chromium, firefox, mobile-chrome) and has NO testMatch/testIgnore filter, so every spec under tests/e2e runs once per project. CI DOES run it: the e2e job invokes `npx playwright test` with no `--project` flag, so all three projects execute. IMPORTANT nuance: mobile.spec.ts does NOT rely on the Pixel-5 viewport of `mobile-chrome` — it overrides the viewport per-describe via `test.use({ viewport: {width,height} })` for 360/390/768 (mobile.spec.ts:60-62). Because there is no project filter, mobile.spec.ts actually runs 3x (once under chromium, once under firefox, once under mobile-chrome), each time re-applying the 360/390/768 viewports. So the @360/390/768 coverage already exists and already executes in CI today.
ci.howTestsRun: Job `e2e` (name: "E2E Tests (Playwright)"), ci.yml:72-100. Steps: checkout, setup-node 20, `npm ci`, `npx playwright install --with-deps chromium firefox`, then `npx playwright test` (ci.yml:91-92), then an artifact upload step guarded by `if: always()`. The job has `needs: [build]` (which `needs: [quality]`), so it is part of the lint→build→e2e chain. The test step has NO `continue-on-error` and NO `if: always()` (only the upload step does), so a Playwright failure fails the `e2e` job and thus the overall workflow run. Whether that BLOCKS A MERGE depends on GitHub branch-protection required-status-checks, which is NOT defined in-repo: there is no .github/settings.yml, no CODEOWNERS, no branch-protection file. So today e2e failure makes the PR's CI "red" but is only merge-blocking if `e2e` (or the workflow) is configured as a required check in the repo's branch-protection settings on GitHub — that cannot be confirmed from the repo and is the real unverified gap. Caveat: `npx playwright install` only installs chromium+firefox; the `mobile-chrome` project uses chromium under the hood, so it still runs — no missing browser.
promoteToBlockingSteps: No code/config change is needed for the spec to RUN at 360/390/768: tests/e2e/mobile.spec.ts is already discovered by `npx playwright test` (no testIgnore) and already self-applies the 360/390/768 viewports via test.use() — so it executes today across chromium, firefox, and mobile-chrome.

Confirm the spec is non-flaky/green in CI before gating: the modal tests dispatch CustomEvents (openMyPacket / openTacticalCalculator / openWorkflowGuide) and poll for an overlay; if the app no longer fires those, the gate would block on a stale test. Run `npx playwright test mobile.spec.ts` in CI conditions once to validate it passes.

Make the gate explicit and bisectable (optional but recommended): mirror the existing `red-team` pattern by adding a dedicated job, e.g. `e2e-mobile`, that runs only the mobile spec: `npx playwright test tests/e2e/mobile.spec.ts --project=mobile-chrome` (add `--project=chromium` too if you want it under desktop engines). Give it `needs: [build]`. A separate job makes a mobile regression visible at a glance rather than buried in the combined e2e run.

If you keep it inside the existing `e2e` job instead of a new job, add a script alias in package.json (e.g. `"test:e2e:mobile": "playwright test tests/e2e/mobile.spec.ts"`) and call it as its own step so failures are labeled.

Ensure the gate is NOT bypassable: verify neither the `e2e` job nor any new mobile job has `continue-on-error: true` (currently none do — only legal-ingestion.yml:50 uses it, unrelated). Do not add `if: always()` to the test step.

THE ACTUAL BLOCKING STEP (must be done in GitHub, not in the repo): add the job to branch protection. On GitHub → Settings → Branches → branch protection rule for `main` → enable 'Require status checks to pass before merging' and add the job's check name ('E2E Tests (Playwright)' and/or the new 'e2e-mobile') to the Required checks list. Without this, a red e2e run does not prevent merge.

Optionally codify branch protection in-repo so it is reviewable: add a `.github/settings.yml` (Probot Settings app) or a Terraform/GH-API script listing the required checks, since no such file exists today.

Optional hardening: pin the 360/390/768 baselines so they cannot silently drift — they are currently hardcoded in mobile.spec.ts:14-18 (small-android 360x740, iphone 390x844, tablet-edge 768x1024), which already matches the owner-specified @360/390/768 requirement, so no change required there.
